text_summary.body: Daniel's reading of PERES announces that the kingdom is given to the Medes and Persians; the chapter ends with Belshazzar's death and Darius the Mede receiving the kingdom. The capture itself is not narrated.

setting.body: Cyrus defeated the army of Akkad at Opis on the Tigris; Sippar was taken on the 14th (11 Oct) without battle and Nabonidus fled; on the 16th (13 Oct in Parker & Dubberstein) Ugbaru and Cyrus's army entered Babylon without battle; Nabonidus was captured; Cyrus entered on 3 Arahsamna (29 Oct) and peace was proclaimed.

competing_reconstructions.label: Peaceful entry (cuneiform sources)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Babylon was entered "without battle"; the Cylinder frames this as Marduk's choice of Cyrus.

competing_reconstructions.label: Surprise entry by the river during a festival (Greek sources)
competing_reconstructions.summary: After a siege, Cyrus diverted the Euphrates and his men entered along the riverbed while the city celebrated; Xenophon adds that the king was killed in his palace.

competing_reconstructions.label: Propaganda and a forced entry
competing_reconstructions.summary: The "without battle" claim is pro-Persian framing; Tolini proposes a forced entry through the Enlil Gate that the river story may echo.

commentary.paraphrase: Guzik follows Herodotus on the diverted Euphrates and unlocked gates and sees the fall as fulfilling Isaiah 44:28–45:7 and Jeremiah 51:57–58.

open_questions: Consult Parker & Dubberstein 1956 to confirm the 1942 conversion.
